Content

ANDHRA PRADESH

  • Ugadi: Telugu New Year; marks the beginning of a new Hindu Lunisolar calendar.
  • Tirupati Brahmotsavam: Annual festival of Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala, celebrated for 9 days.
  • Durgamma Festival: celebrated in Durga Pooja.
  • Visakha Utsav: held in December.
  • Yellama Jatara
  • Sankranti (Pedda Panduga)

ARUNACHAL PRADESH

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Arun kya tere Sang Solun is Tree ke neeche Chalo Sir Meri Pin pakdo aur Paas aao

  • Arun → Arunachal Pradesh
  • Sang → Sangken; a 3 day festival celebrated in April.
  • Solun → Solung; a 10 day harvest festival celebrated by 'Adi Tribe'.
  • Tree → Dree Festival; celebrated by Apatani tribe in the month of July.
  • Cha → Chalo Loku: celebrated by Nocte tribe in July/August.
  • Lo Sir → Losar: New Year Festival of Tibetan Buddhism, celebrated by Monpa tribe, marks the 1st day of Tibetan calendar.
  • Meri Pin → Mopin: celebrated by Galo tribe in April.
  • Paas aao → Pangsau: to honour the war heroes who died in WW2.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Ziro Festival: founded in 2012.
  • Boori-Boot: celebrated by Nyishi Tribe.

ASSAM

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Assam ki Bahu ne Bai ko Patak patak ke mara kyunki usko Ali ke Abbu ke saath Majuli Festival dekhne jana tha.

  • Bahu → Bihu, celebrated thrice a year
  • Rongali/Bohag Bihu: in April, marks beginning of Assam's New Year.
  • Kati/Kongali Bihu: in Oct-Nov.
  • Bhogali/Magh Bihu: in January.
  • Baiko → Baikho: celebrated by Rabha Community, pre-harvest; Baishagu festival.
  • Patak → Dehing Patkai: a 3-day annual festival held in January at Lekhapani in Tinsukia district.
  • Ali → Ali Ai Ligang: Harvest festival of Mishing Tribe.
  • Abbu → Ambubachi: held at Kamakhya temple.
  • Marks the Menstrual phase of Goddess Kamakhya.
  • Also known as Ameti/ Tantric fertility Festival.
  • Majuli → Majuli: a 3-day festival held in November.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Rongker Festival: celebrated by Karbi Tribe.
  • Junbeel Mela: exchange of products through Barter exchange.

BIHAR

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Sonu Shaam ko Chhath par Bahu La

  • Sonu → Sonepur Cattle Fair: one of Asia's largest Cattle Fairs, held in November.
  • Shaam → Sama Chakeva: originates from Mithila region.
  • Chhath → Chhath Pooja: to honour the Sun God and Chhathi Maiya, in the month of Kartika.
  • Bahu La → Bihula: celebrated in the month of August; devotees pray to the Serpent Goddess Mansa.
  • Rajgir Festival: 3 days festival, started in 1986.

CHHATTISGARH

TRICK TO REMEMBER: 36 Madai Soncha aur Bola Haveli me Basta leke Dussehra Manaenge

  • 36 → Chhattisgarh
  • Madai → Madai: celebrated by Gond tribe.
  • Soncha → Goncha: The Chariot festival of tribes of Bastar district celebrated for 9 days.
  • Bola → Pola: a thanksgiving festival, to acknowledge the importance of Bulls & Oxen.
  • also celebrated in Maharashtra.
  • Haveli → Hareli: a Harvest festival of Shravan month (July/August).
  • Basta Dussehra → Bastar Dussehra: to honour Goddess Danteshwari.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Karam: tribute to Karam Tree, a harvest festival.
  • Champaran Mela: an annual fair held in Champaran region, Raipur.
  • Narayanpur Mela.

GOA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: 3 Kings went to Goa's St. Francis Xavier church took some Grapes lekin Car Nahi mili aur Sunburn ho Gaya.

  • 3 Kings → 3 Kinga Festival: also known as Epiphany festival.
  • St. Francis Xavier → Feast of Saint Francis Xavier: celebrated on 3rd December - Death anniversary of Saint Francis.
  • Grapes → Grapes Escapade.
  • Car Nahi → Carnival.
  • Sunburn → Sunburn.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Shigmo: Shigmotsav/Shishirotsava is a spring festival celebrated in Falgun month of the Hindu calendar.
  • Sao Jao.
  • Bonderam: celebrated on 4th Saturday of every August in the Divar Island.
  • Chikal Kalo: a mud festival that celebrates Lord Krishna's childhood, in the Devaki Krishna temple of Marcel, Goa.

GUJARAT

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Sharma Ji Madhav se Karva Chauth pe Rann kar rahe the.

  • SharmaJi → Shamlaji Melo: celebrated in November for 3 weeks, dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
  • Madhav → Madhavpur mela: celebrates marriage of Lord Krishna and Rukmini, in the Porbandar district of Gujarat.
  • Modhera Dance Festival: celebrated at Modhera Sun temple (Mehsana district) for 3 days in the 3rd week of January.
  • Chauth → Vautha Mela: an Animal trading festival.
  • Rann → Rann Utsav: also known as White desert Festival, continues for 3 months in the Great Rann of Kutch.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Dang Darbar: a tribal festival celebrated just before Holi.
  • Chitra Vichitra Fair.
  • Bhavnath Fair.
  • Dhrang Fair.

HIMACHAL PRADESH

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Him Pari ko Haldi aur Phul se Saza do Kalinjar ke Raja aa rahe hain.

  • Him → Himachal Pradesh.
  • Pari → Pori: also known as Horse Festival.
  • Haldi → Halda: celebrated in Lahaul Spiti Valley.
  • Phul → Phulaich: also known as Ukyam Festival is a festival of flowers.
  • Saza → Sazo: celebrated in Kinnaur Valley.
  • Sair festival.
  • Kalinjar → Minjar Fair: held in town of Chamba for one week.

HARYANA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Suraj ki Pin Ganga me Gum ho gayi.

  • Suraj → Surajkund festival: held in Faridabad.
  • Pin → Pinjore.
  • Ganga → Gugga Navami: dedicated to Gugga Pir, worship of snakes.
  • Gum → Gangaur: dedicated to Goddess Gauri or Parvati; is also celebrated in Rajasthan & Madhya Pradesh.

JHARKHAND

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Rohini ka Bhagta Sohar, usko Susu lagi aur usne ye Karam Sarhad pe kar diya.

  • Rohini → Rohini: marks the beginning of sowing season.
  • Bhagta → Bhagta Parab: to honour Budha Baba celebrated by indigenous tribes of Jharkhand.
  • Sohar → Sohrai: a harvest festival, celebrated on the new moon day of Kartik.
  • Susu → Tusu Parab: held on the last day of Hindu month Paush.
  • Karam → Karam: to honour Karam Devta - God of Power and Youthfulness, for a good harvest.
  • Sarhad → Sarhul: marks the arrival of Spring.
  • Jawa: a celebration of fertility, by unmarried tribal girls.

KARNATAKA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Humara kaam wala Abhishek kal apne abba ke sath gaadi Karke aya tha.

  • Humara → Hampi festival: also known as 'Vijay Utsav'.
  • Kaam wala → Kambala: a buffalo race event.
  • Abhishek → Mahamastya Abhishek: held every 12 years. Anointment of the Bahubali Gommateshwara statue located at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
  • Kal → Pattadakal Dance Festival.
  • Kailpodh festival: Worshipping of arms and Weapons, celebrated by Kodava community of Kodagu district.
  • (Right column continues Karnataka) Abba → Gombe Habba: Festival of dolls, 10 days celebration during Navratri.
  • Gowri Habba.
  • Gaadi → Ugadi: New Year Festival.
  • Karke → Karga: a festival dedicated to Draupadi.

KERALA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Pooram Vasu they are at Pain because they lost Boat Race on Makar Sankranti.

  • Pooram → Thrissur Pooram: held at Vadakkumnathan temple.
  • Vasu → Vishu: New Year Festival.
  • They → Theyyam: celebrated mostly in North Malabar.
  • Are → Arattu.
  • At → Attukal Pongal.
  • Pain → Painkuni: celebrated at Padmanabha Swamy temple.
  • Boat race → Vallam Kalli Boat Race.
  • On → Onam: A harvest festival, welcomes the return of Asura Mahabali.
  • Makar Sankranti → Makar Vilakku: held at Sabarimala temple, dedicated to lord Ayyappa.

MADHYA PRADESH

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Ghade me Rang lagake Khajur ka Ras dalke Nagmani rakhke Ganga ke Madhya Gira do aur Bhag jao.

  • Ghade → Ghadlya: celebrated in the month of Aug-Sept.
  • Rang → Lokrang: commences on Republic Day.
  • Khajur → Khajuraho: held in Chhatarpur district.
  • Ras → Ras Nawa: celebrated by Baigas of Mandla district.
  • Nagmani → Panchmarhi Utsav: a 6 day festival.
  • Ganga → Gangaur.
  • Gira → Chethiyagiri Vihara: to worship the relics of Sariputta and Mahamogallena, in Sanchi, MP.
  • Bhag → Bhagoria Haat: a harvest festival in spring season.
  • Malwa Utsav is also celebrated in MP.

MANIPUR

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Mani aate hi apne Sang Doll and Cherry lai fir Hindon me Nhai.

  • Mani → Manipur.
  • Sang → Kang Jatra Kut.
  • doll → Dol Jatra (Yaosang): known as 'Holi' of Manipur.
  • Cherry → Cherry Blossom.
  • lai → Lai Haroba: by Meitei tribe to honour Umang Lais, a sacred tree.
  • Hindon → Heirku Hidongba.
  • Nhai → Lui Ngai Ni, Gang Ngai.

NAGALAND

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Nag Bill me Aao, Muh se sakkar khao.

  • Nag → Nagaland.
  • Bill → Hornbill: celebrated from 1-10 December.
  • Aao → Aoleang: celebrated in the 1st week of April by the Konyak Naga people.
  • Muh → Moatsu: celebrated by Ao Tribe.
  • Sakkar → Sekrenyi: annual festival of the Angami Nagas.

MEGHALAYA

  • Shad Suk Mynsiem.
  • Nongkrem Festival: by Khasi Tribe.
  • Behdienkhlam Festival: by Jaintia Tribe.
  • Shad Sukra.
  • Wangala Festival: by Garo Tribe (aka Festival of Festivals).
  • Strawberry Festival.
  • Cherry Blossom Festival.

ODISHA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: 6 Khai ya Nau Khai, ye Kaun batayega? Kalinga ke Raja Jo Rath pe baithe hain.

  • Nau Khai → Nua Khai.
  • Kaun → Konark Festival: a 5 day Dance festival held from (1-5) Dec.
  • Kalinga → Kalinga Mahotsav: 2 day long event.
  • Raja → Raja Prabha.
  • Rath → Rath Yatra.

Some Other Festivals:

  • Chhau.
  • Bal Yatra.

MIZORAM

  • Chapchar Kut.
  • Mim Kut.
  • Phawang Kut.

PUNJAB

  • Hola Mohalla: celebrated a day after Holi.
  • Guru Purab: celebrates the birth of Guru Nanak - 1st Sikh Guru.
  • Lohri: a part of Makar Sankranti.
  • Baisakhi: commemorates the formation of Khalsa Panth.

MAHARASHTRA

  • Vithoba: dedicated to 'Vitthal' form of Lord Vishnu.
  • Gudi Padwa: symbolises the victory of good over evil.
  • Kala Ghoda Mahotsav: 9 days long art festival.
  • Narali Purnima.
  • Banganga.
  • Vat Purnima.
  • Kojagiri.
  • Ganesh Chaturthi.
  • Elephanta festival.
  • Pola festival.
  • Palkhi festival.

RAJASTHAN

  • Pushkar Fair: A Camel fair in Ajmer.
  • Gangaur: dedicated to Goddess Gauri.
  • Desert festival: celebrated in Jaisalmer.
  • Nagaur fair: a cattle fair.
  • Chandrabhaga fair: held in Kartik month (Oct-Nov).
  • Bundi Utsav: held in Kartik month (Oct-Nov).
  • Baneshwar: Bhil tribe, dedicated to Baneshwar Mahadev (lord Shiva).
  • Kolayat fair: also known as Kapil Muni fair, held in Bikaner during Kartik Purnima.

SIKKIM

  • Losoong: Bhutia tribe.
  • Namsoong: Lepcha tribe.
  • Losar: New Year Festival.
  • Sakewa: annual 9 day festival by Kirat Khambu Rai Community.
  • Pang Lhabsol: Chu Faat a sacred folk dance is performed by the Lepcha tribe of Sikkim during the Pang Lhabsol festival. It signifies the worship of 5 sacred peaks - Mt. Kanchenjunga, Mt. Kabru, Mt. Simbrum, Mt. Pandim, and Mt. Narshing.
  • Sonam Lochar / Tamu Lochar.
  • Saga Dawa: also known as Triple Blessed festival.

TAMIL NADU

  • Pongal: means 'to boil'.
  • Bhogi Pongal
  • Thai Pongal
  • Mattu Pongal
  • Kaanum Pongal
  • During the Pongal festival, Kolam Rangoli is drawn at the entrance of homes.
  • Jallikattu: Bull Fighting Event.
  • Puthandu: New Year Festival.
  • Natyanjali.
  • Karthigai Deepam.
  • Thaipusam: to worship lord Murugan, Kavadi is carried.
  • Mahamaham: known as 'Kumbh of South'; celebrated once every 12 years.

TELANGANA

TRICK TO REMEMBER: Bathua Banalu Sam me Padunga.

  • Bathua → Bathukamma: a 9 day flower festival celebrated by women.
  • Banalu → Bonalu: to honour goddess Mahakali.
  • Sam → Sammak Jatara also known as Medaram Jatara: rituals of this festival is performed by Koya tribe.
  • Padunga → Dunnapothula Panduga: also known as Sadar festival; celebrated by Yadava Community.

TRIPURA

  • Kharchi Puja.
  • Hojagiri: celebrated by Reang community to worship Goddess Mailuma (Laxmi).
  • Garia Puja.
  • Bijhu: celebrated by Chakma tribe, to celebrate new year.

UTTARAKHAND

  • Harela — Celebrated in Kumaon region.
  • Bhitauli — Celebrated in Kumaon region.
  • Syaldey Bikhauli Mela — Celebrated in Kumaon region.
  • Phool dei.
  • Kale Kauva (Ghugutiya).
  • Kandali.
  • Ganga Dussehra.

WEST BENGAL

  • Poila Boisakh: New Year.
  • Durga Puja.
  • Kali Puja.
  • Dol Purnima / Dol Jatra.

Key concepts

  • Bihu (Rongali, Kati, Bhogali)
  • Bastar Dussehra
  • Hornbill Festival
  • Rath Yatra
  • Pongal (Bhogi, Thai, Mattu, Kaanum)
  • Onam
  • Hampi Utsava / Pattadakal Dance Festival
  • Thrissur Pooram

Verified and Edited 2025

Verification date: 2025-12-15

OCR Artifacts Fixed

  • No stray column separators, mojibake characters, or broken line breaks found in body text.

Factual Verifications

  • Andhra Pradesh: Ugadi (Telugu New Year), Tirupati Brahmotsavam (9 days), Durgamma, Visakha Utsav (Dec), Yellama Jatara, Sankranti (Pedda Panduga) — verified.
  • Arunachal Pradesh: Sangken (3 days, April), Solung (10 days, Adi tribe), Dree (Apatani, July), Chalo Loku (Nocte, July/Aug), Losar (Monpa, Tibetan New Year), Mopin (Galo, April), Pangsau (WW2 heroes) — verified.
  • Assam: Bihu (Rongali/Bohag April, Kati/Kongali Oct-Nov, Bhogali/Magh Jan), Baikho (Rabha), Dehing Patkai (3 days Jan, Tinsukia), Ali Ai Ligang (Mishing), Ambubachi (Kamakhya temple, menstrual/fertility festival), Majuli (3 days, Nov) — verified.
  • Bihar: Sonepur Cattle Fair (Asia's largest, Nov), Sama Chakeva (Mithila), Chhath Pooja (Sun God & Chhathi Maiya, Kartika month), Bihula (Aug, serpent goddess Mansa) — verified.
  • Chhattisgarh: Madai (Gond), Goncha (Bastar, 9 days), Pola (thanksgiving for bulls, also in Maharashtra), Hareli (Shravan, harvest), Bastar Dussehra (75-day, Goddess Danteshwari) — verified.
  • Goa: 3 Kinga/Epiphany, Feast of St. Francis Xavier (3 Dec), Grapes Escapade, Carnival, Sunburn, Shigmo (spring, Falgun), Sao Jao, Bonderam (4th Sat of Aug, Divar), Chikal Kalo (mud festival, Devaki Krishna temple) — verified.
  • Gujarat: Shamlaji Melo (Nov, 3 weeks, Lord Vishnu), Madhavpur Mela (Krishna-Rukmini marriage, Porbandar), Modhera Dance Festival (3rd week Jan), Vautha Mela (animal trading), Rann Utsav (3 months, Great Rann of Kutch, "White Desert Festival") — verified.
  • Himachal Pradesh: Pori (Horse Festival), Halda (Lahaul-Spiti), Phulaich (Ukyam, flowers), Sazo (Kinnaur), Minjar Fair (Chamba, 1 week) — verified.
  • Haryana: Surajkund (Faridabad), Pinjore, Gugga Navami (snake worship), Gangaur (also Rajasthan & MP) — verified.
  • Jharkhand: Rohini (sowing), Bhagta Parab (Budha Baba), Sohrai (Kartik new moon), Tusu Parab (Paush end), Karam (Karam Devta, harvest), Sarhul (spring) — verified.
  • Karnataka: Hampi (Vijay Utsav), Kambala (buffalo race), Mahamastya Abhishek (every 12 years, Shravanabelagola), Pattadakal Dance Festival, Kailpodh (Kodagu, arms worship), Gombe Habba (dolls, 10 days Navratri), Gowri Habba, Ugadi, Karga (Draupadi) — verified.
  • Kerala: Thrissur Pooram (Vadakkumnathan), Vishu (New Year), Theyyam (North Malabar), Arattu, Attukal Pongal, Painkuni (Padmanabha Swamy), Vallam Kalli (boat race), Onam (Mahabali return), Makar Vilakku (Sabarimala, Ayyappa) — verified.
  • Madhya Pradesh: Ghadlya (Aug-Sept), Lokrang (Republic Day), Khajuraho (Chhatarpur), Ras Nawa (Baigas, Mandla), Panchmarhi Utsav (6 days), Gangaur, Chethiyagiri Vihara (Sanchi), Bhagoria Haat (spring harvest), Malwa Utsav — verified.
  • Manipur: Kang Jatra Kut, Dol Jatra/Yaosang (Holi of Manipur), Cherry Blossom, Lai Haroba (Meitei, Umang Lais tree), Heirku Hidongba, Lui Ngai Ni, Gang Ngai — verified.
  • Meghalaya: Shad Suk Mynsiem, Nongkrem (Khasi), Behdienkhlam (Jaintia), Wangala (Garo, "Festival of 100 Drums"/Festival of Festivals), Strawberry, Cherry Blossom — verified.
  • Nagaland: Hornbill (1-10 Dec), Aoleang (1st week Apr, Konyak), Moatsu (Ao), Sekrenyi (Angami) — verified.
  • Odisha: Nua Khai, Konark Festival (1-5 Dec, 5-day dance), Kalinga Mahotsav, Raja Prabha, Rath Yatra — verified.
  • Punjab: Hola Mohalla (day after Holi), Guru Purab (Guru Nanak), Lohri (Makar Sankranti), Baisakhi (Khalsa Panth) — verified.
  • Rajasthan: Pushkar Fair (Ajmer, camel), Gangaur (Goddess Gauri), Desert (Jaisalmer), Nagaur (cattle), Chandrabhaga (Kartik), Bundi Utsav (Kartik), Baneshwar (Bhil, Lord Shiva), Kolayat (Kapil Muni fair, Bikaner, Kartik Purnima) — verified.
  • Sikkim: Losoong (Bhutia), Namsoong (Lepcha), Losar, Sakewa (9 days, Kirat Khambu Rai), Pang Lhabsol (Chu Faat dance, 5 sacred peaks), Sonam Lochar/Tamu Lochar, Saga Dawa ("Triple Blessed") — verified.
  • Tamil Nadu: Pongal (Bhogi, Thai, Mattu, Kaanum), Jallikattu (bull fighting), Puthandu (New Year), Natyanjali, Karthigai Deepam, Thaipusam (Murugan, Kavadi), Mahamaham ("Kumbh of South," every 12 years) — verified.
  • Telangana: Bathukamma (9 days, women, flowers), Bonalu (Mahakali), Sammak Jatara/Medaram Jatara (Koya tribe, Chaitra), Dunnapothula Panduga (Sadar, Yadava) — verified.
  • Tripura: Kharchi Puja, Hojagiri (Reang, Goddess Mailuma/Laxmi), Garia Puja, Bijhu (Chakma, New Year) — verified.
  • Uttarakhand: Harela, Bhitauli, Syaldey Bikhauli Mela, Phool Dei, Kale Kauva/Ghugutiya, Kandali, Ganga Dussehra (all Kumaon region) — verified.
  • West Bengal: Poila Boisakh, Durga Puja, Kali Puja, Dol Purnima/Dol Jatra — verified.
